content: 1. BJOG published a study in 2016 (Volume 123, Issue 4, Pages 529-539) focusing on healthy pregnant women. 2. Zakiyah N, Postma MJ, Baker PN, and van Asselt AD, as part of the Consortium I, conducted a review of published economic assessments regarding the diagnosis and treatment options for pre-eclampsia. This was published in PharmacoEconomics in 2015 (Volume 33, Issue 10, Pages 1069-1082). 3. Werner EF, Hauspurg AK, and Rouse DJ performed a cost-benefit analysis of low-dose aspirin prophylaxis for the prevention of preeclampsia in the United States. This study was published in Obstetrics & Gynecology. 4. Mallampati D, Grobman W, Rouse DJ, and Werner EF analyzed strategies for prescribing aspirin to prevent preeclampsia through a cost-effectiveness lens. Their findings were published in Obstetrics & Gynecology in September 2019 (Volume 134, Issue 3, Pages 537-544). 5. Cuckle H also explored strategies for prescribing aspirin to prevent preeclampsia, focusing on cost-effectiveness. This analysis was published in Obstetrics & Gynecology in January 2020 (Volume 135, Issue 1, Page 217). 6. Ortved D, Hawkins TL, Johnson JA, Hyett J, and Metcalfe A evaluated the cost-effectiveness of first-trimester screening combined with early preventive aspirin use in women at high risk of early-onset preeclampsia. Their study appeared in Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology in 2019 (Volume 53, Issue 2, Pages 239-244). 7. Mone F, O’Mahony JF, Tyrrell E, Mulcahy C, McParland P, Breathnach F, and colleagues compared routine aspirin use versus screening test-indicated aspirin use for preeclampsia prevention in low-risk women. This study was published in Hypertension in December 2018 (Volume 72, Issue 6, Pages 1391-1396). 8. Arsenault C, Jordan K, Lee D, Dinsa G, Manzi F, Marchant T, and others analyzed equity in antenatal care quality using data from 91 national household surveys. Their findings were published in The Lancet Global Health in 2018 (Volume 6, Issue 11, Pages e1186-e1195). 9. Mone F, Mulcahy C, McParland P, Breathnach F, Downey P, and colleagues conducted the TEST study, a multicenter randomized controlled trial assessing the feasibility and acceptability of routine low-dose aspirin versus early screening test-indicated aspirin for preeclampsia prevention. This was published in BMJ Open on July 28, 2018 (Volume 8, Issue 7, Article e022056). 10. Downe S, Finlayson K, Tunçalp Ö, and Gülmezoglu AM synthesized qualitative evidence on the provision and uptake of routine antenatal services. This review was published in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2019 (Issue 6). 11. The World Health Organization released the 21st Model List of Essential Medicines in 2019, which includes key recommendations for global health priorities.
